text:
Arseny Gritsyuk has eight goals in his second NHL season, and Sheldon Keefe has started using him on a line with Jesper Bratt and Jack Hughes to flip momentum, per The Hockey News. That's a big vote of confidence for a fifth-round pick who came over from SKA St. Petersburg.

All About The Jersey asked whether he can keep up this scoring pace, and the honest answer is no, not quite. He's shooting 18%, double last season's 9%, and New Jersey has scored 5.3 more goals than expected with him on. The chances are real, though (5.0 expected goals), and the Devils take 62% of the expected goals at five on five with him out there.

He plays fast: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries, with more than half his shots off the rush. Our range has him at 21 to 34 goals, which would still be a big step.
